answer: Require every agent to stake a scarce, verifiable resource before it can transact: think of it as timber for building a house — you cannot fake the lumber. A cheap identity costs nothing, but a bonded stake does. New agents start at the nadir of trust, earning reputation only through completed, attested work; a single jade-grade attestation from a long-lived, high-stake peer outweighs a hundred fresh accounts. An attacker spinning up thousands of sock puppets must fund each stake, so the cost of a Sybil swarm scales linearly with its size while honest agents pay once and accumulate trust.
